behavioral_evidence.value: Directed consecutive-item transitions from the train split only, aggregated as C[i,j] and symmetrised into an undirected behaviour graph W = C + C^T.

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: For every session in the train split, count consecutive pairs (i_t, i_{t+1}) into C; row-normalise nothing (raw counts), build the symmetric normalised adjacency A = D_r^{-1/2} (C+C^T) D_c^{-1/2}, take the top m=32 eigenpairs (lambda_k, u_k) by magnitude with Lanczos, set g_i = (lambda_k u_k[i])_{k=1..32}, rho_i = ||g_i||, r_i = r_max * clip(rho_i / q90(rho), r_min/r_max, 1) with r_max = artanh(0.9) and r_min = artanh(0.2), and v_i = r_i g_i/||g_i||, v_i = 0 if rho_i = 0. All of this is computed from train interactions only, before Stage2 starts, and is frozen.

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: BEHAV_SMOOTH = False, CURV_C = 1.0: eta_i = 0 for every item, so b_i = z_i and the run is the round-one frozen-geometry curved residual chain exactly; the pipeline executes the same code path with the tangent sum multiplied by zero, so the switch is verifiably wired. Not trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: BEHAV_SMOOTH = True, CURV_C = 1.0: the single trained arm, b_i = exp_{z_i}(eta_i sum_j w_ij log_{z_i}(z_j)) on the unit ball, followed by the frozen 3000-epoch Stage-2 recipe and the frozen Stage-3 protocol. One run, no tuning, no seed repetition.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: BEHAV_SMOOTH = True, CURV_C = 0.0: the ball is replaced by flat R^32, z_i = kappa t_i, log_z(w) = w - z, and b_i = z_i + eta_i sum_j w_ij (z_j - z_i), i.e. the identical behaviour weights and the identical concentration applied as an arithmetic blend inside a Euclidean RQ-VAE. Not trained in this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the Stage-2 training sequences only (the interaction sequences used to train the RQ-VAE), truncated at the Stage-2 split boundary: for every position t add 1.0 to C[i_t, i_{t+1}] and 0.5 to C[i_t, i_{t+2}]; drop self-pairs; row-normalise to p_ij; divide by p_j^{1/2} using item frequencies counted on the same training events; renormalise to w_ij; eta_i = sum_j w_ij^2 is the Herfindahl concentration of that row. Items with no outgoing transition in the training split get eta_i = 0 and are counted in a diagnostic.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item transitions with a one-step skip, weighted and popularity-adjusted (a sequential-co-consumption signal), collapsed per item into a normalised successor distribution w_ij and its concentration eta_i.
ideas.cost_estimate: One static precompute and zero per-step cost. Precompute: build the lag-1/lag-2 sparse count matrix from the training sequences (order 10^6 nonzeros), row-normalise, popularity-adjust, then one log map per nonzero plus one exp map per item, over d = 32: roughly 1.5e6 x ~150 flops ~ 2e8 flops, a few seconds on one GPU, and a 24,556 x 32 float32 table (3.1 MB). At the frozen scale (24,556 training items, 24 steps/epoch, 4096 global batch, 3000 epochs = 72,000 steps) the added per-step cost is a single row-gather: 0 FLOPs, 0 added communication, no change to DDP bucket sizes. Stage2 wall clock therefore stays at the measured 571 s / 0.145 s per epoch plus about 5 s of precompute (<1%); Stage3 is untouched at 150 epochs.
ideas.coupling_equation: b_i = exp_{z_i}( eta_behaviour(i) * sum_j w_behaviour(i,j) * log_{z_i}(z_j) ), with eta_behaviour(i) = sum_j w_behaviour(i,j)^2, all maps taken on the Poincare ball of curvature c = 1; behaviour enters through w and eta, curvature through the basepoint-dependent exp/log at z_i in B_c.
ideas.coupling_path: behaviour counts -> row-normalised, popularity-adjusted weights w_ij and concentration eta_i -> tangent vector v_i = sum_j w_ij log_{z_i}(z_j) -> geodesic step b_i = exp_{z_i}(eta_i v_i) -> level-1 assignment -> residual -> level-2, level-3 codes -> SID tokens -> Stage-3 sequence model. The behaviour term sets both the direction and the length of a curved displacement, and the curved term sets what that displacement means geometrically; setting eta_i = 0 deletes the whole pathway (b_i = z_i, the baseline input), and setting c = 0 turns the same weights into a flat blend, which changes the length and the landing point of every step for every item at radius > 0. Neither removal leaves the core computation intact.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: What must be true is that (i) items with a concentrated, popularity-adjusted successor distribution are exactly the items whose text latent is a poor guide to their next-item role (serialised content, tightly coupled co-consumption), and (ii) the curved step damps far moves more than a flat blend would, because items already near the ball boundary would otherwise be pushed onto their neighbour's prefix and collapse level-1 usage. If both hold, moving those items onto the geodesic toward their successors' tangent barycentre raises prefix-level predictability (the level-3 token becomes predictable from levels 1-2 and the last item) while the boundary damping keeps the partition spread out. Observed as: level-1 active codewords stay >= 240, distinct L2/L3 prefixes stay >= 1,700, within-prefix behaviour dispersion drops, between-prefix contrast rises, and Stage3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065 in the single frozen run.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In quantization only, at the input of level 1: the item latents that the residual quantizer partitions are moved in the ball before the first assignment, and because the level-1 assignment, the residual and hence the level-2 and level-3 codes are all functions of that input, the curved step re-partitions all three levels. No change to the encoder, the decoder, the losses, the codebook dimension, the number of codewords or the Stage-3 model.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed negative curvature c = 1 on the unit Poincare ball: the exponential map exp_{z}(.) anchored at the item's own position, the logarithmic map log_{z}(.) to that tangent space, the induced Poincare distance d_B, and the resulting geodesic convex combination exp_{z}(eta * log_z(mu)). Curvature is fixed, not tuned; the mechanism makes no claim about curvature magnitude (issue 126 showed curvature is a gauge), it uses the basepoint-dependent exp/log pair, which is precisely what does not exist at c = 0.
ideas.key_change: Replace the frozen per-item latent z_i that feeds the RQ chain by b_i = exp_{z_i}( eta_i * sum_j w_ij log_{z_i}(z_j) ), where w_ij are popularity-adjusted directed-transition weights computed from the Stage-2 training split only and eta_i = sum_j w_ij^2 is the measured concentration. Nothing else in Stage2 or Stage3 changes.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Every count, every frequency, every row of w and every eta_i is computed from training-split interactions only; validation and test sequences are never opened, and the Stage-3 test queries are not touched at any point of SID construction. The text latents t_i are the frozen Stage-1 outputs built from item metadata, which contain no interaction data at all. No user identifier and no held-out interaction enters the table; the table is built once, before Stage2 starts, and is frozen for the whole 3000 epochs, so no feedback from Stage-2 or Stage-3 loss can reach it.
ideas.motivation: The SID is currently determined by where an item's text latent happens to sit in the ball. That geometry knows nothing about what the item is followed by, so at depth three 24,556 items are compressed into 2,201 prefixes (~11 items each) whose members are textually similar but behaviourally unrelated; Stage3 then has to spend prefix tokens discriminating items that the prefix says are the same, or predicting a next item whose prefix is not the prefix that behaviour would have chosen. Issue 126 says the recall-predictive structure is behaviour-CONTRAST (within-group tightness plus between-group separation), not Gromov-delta and not ancestor depth, so the fix has to be a partition change driven by directed behaviour contrast, not another additive loss.
ideas.novelty: Different coupling position from everything already tried here. The rejected/prior mechanisms changed (a) codebook centroids via successor-weighted Frechet means, (b) per-level curvature from hard prefix-transition scores, (c) the radial coordinate by context entropy, (d) Lorentz successor-profile smoothing of the codebook, (e) a behaviour cone on prefixes, (f) a successor boost shift. This one leaves the codebooks, the loss and the encoder completely untouched and instead moves the QUANTIZER INPUT: each item is transported along the geodesic toward the tangent-mean of the items that actually follow it, by a step size equal to the measured concentration (Herfindahl) of its own popularity-adjusted transition distribution. There is no origin-minimising objective (the round-one collapse mode), because nothing is optimised: it is a deterministic, closed-form, once-per-run input transformation. No Gromov delta, no ancestor-depth weight, no tree premise. The curvature is not a scale gauge here: the operation is a basepoint-dependent exponential map at each item's own position, which has no flat counterpart at equal step size.
ideas.observables: (1) SID assignment: the fraction of items whose level-3 code differs from the code that their unsmoothed z_i would receive under the trained codebooks (computed post hoc, no training) should be large, target > 0.20; (2) prefix structure: level-1 active codewords, distinct L2 and L3 prefix counts must stay in band (L1 >= 240, L2 >= 1,700, L3 >= 1,700, no duplicate SIDs after repair); (3) prefix behaviour predictability: mean total-variation distance between the successor distributions of items sharing a level-3 prefix should fall and the mean between-prefix TV should rise, and the entropy of the level-3 token given (level-1, level-2, last item) on the training sequences should fall; (4) radial structure: the correlation between prefix-group mean radius and prefix-group behaviour dispersion should be more negative than in the text-only partition, matching the group-compactness finding of issue 126; (5) Stage3: test_recall@10 against the 0.065 gate, with recall@5 and ndcg@10 recorded.

rejected_ideas.reason: out of scope: ablation_geometry_off does not say what replaces the curve

risks: The concentration step may be tiny for most items (diffuse real-world transition distributions), in which case b_i ~ z_i, the SID is effectively unchanged and the run reproduces round one's 0.054; the eta histogram and the SID-change fraction are recorded for exactly this reason. Popularity adjustment with exponent 1/2 may be too weak, so many items are pulled onto the same hub and level-1/level-3 prefix counts fall. Because the geometry is frozen, the mechanism can only repartition the existing Stage-1 geometry, which round one showed yields a modest ceiling; the step is not allowed to fix a bad text geometry, only to re-aim it. Curvature may turn out to be a near-gauge for the smoothed points (the flat and curved midpoints differ only at second order for small steps), in which case the geometry contributes little; since no geometry-off arm is trained, this is recorded as an untested risk, not an admission gate. Duplicate SIDs could appear where two items share a dominant successor; a deterministic one-pass repair is specified. Finally, the whole mechanism depends on the transition matrix being informative for cold items, which it is not; those keep eta_i = 0.
ideas.safeguards: (a) atanh argument clipped at 0.9999 and the Moebius denominator floored at 1e-8, so no log map can blow up; (b) the tangent step is norm-clipped to 0.995 and the result re-projected to radius 0.995, so no point reaches the boundary and the exp map never saturates; (c) eta_i is bounded in [1/|S_i|, 1] by construction and is exactly 0 for items with no training transitions, so every step is a contraction toward a neighbour and never an extrapolation past it; (d) popularity adjustment with exponent 1/2 (documented BM25-style default) prevents hub collapse, and level-1 active-codeword count and distinct L2/L3 prefix counts are logged every 100 epochs to expose collapse early; (e) all arithmetic in float32 with the ball radius checked after every exp map; (f) duplicate-SID repair: if two items share a (q1,q2,q3) triple the item with the larger eta_i keeps it and the other item takes the next-nearest level-3 codeword under the same Poincare distance, in a single deterministic pass, with the number of repaired items reported; (g) the table is built once and frozen, so no run-to-run drift and no dependence on the Stage-2 batch order.
ideas.spec_equations:
pseudocode for the precompute:
  read training sequences; for each sequence s, for t in range(len(s)-2):
      C[s[t], s[t+1]] += 1.0 ; C[s[t], s[t+2]] += 0.5
  for i: C[i,i] = 0
  freq[j] = column_sum(C)[j] ; p_j = freq[j]/freq.sum()
  for each row i with row_sum(C[i]) > 0:
      p_ij = C[i,j]/row_sum(C[i])
      a_ij = p_ij / sqrt(max(p_j, eps))
      w_ij = a_ij / a_i.sum()
      eta_i = sum_j w_ij^2
  else eta_i = 0
  kappa = 0.9 / max_i ||t_i||
  Z = [exp_0(kappa t_i) for i]                     # unit ball, c=1, radius tanh(0.9) <= 0.717
  for i:
      V[i] = sum_j w_ij * log_{Z[i]}(Z[j])         # tangent at Z[i]
      V[i] = clip_norm(V[i], max_norm = 0.995)     # artanh(0.995) safety
      B[i] = exp_{Z[i]}(eta_i * V[i])
      if ||B[i]|| > 0.995: B[i] = B[i] * 0.995/||B[i]||
  save B as the frozen item input table
  Stage2: for 3000 epochs, 24 steps of global batch 4096, feed B[i] to the existing 3x256 curved RQ-VAE, unchanged loss
  Stage3: frozen protocol, unchanged
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: the frozen Stage-1 item text latents t_i in R^32 (one row per training item), the Stage-2 training interaction sequences, the curvature constant c = 1 and the two switches. Outputs: one 24,556 x 32 float32 table B of smoothed ball coordinates, consumed in place of the text latents by the unchanged RQ-VAE; plus diagnostics (eta histogram, per-item support size, count of eta = 0 items). The operator is deterministic and idempotent at fixed inputs; it is computed once before Stage2 and never recomputed.

specification.text:
Geometry, fixed curvature c = 1, unit Poincare ball B = {x in R^32 : ||x|| < 1}.
  scale: kappa = 0.9 / max_i ||t_i||  (t_i = frozen Stage-1 text latent, d = 32), computed once, so every point starts inside radius tanh(0.9) = 0.716.
  z_i = exp_0(kappa t_i) = tanh(kappa||t_i||) * t_i/||t_i||.
  log_z(w) = d_B(z,w) * (w (-) z)/||w (-) z||, with Moebius difference (w (-) z) = ((1-||z||^2)w - (1-2<z,w>+||w||^2)z) / (1-2<z,w>+||z||^2||w||^2) and d_B(z,w) = 2*atanh(||w (-) z||).
  exp_z(u) = z (+) tanh(||u||) * u/||u||  (Moebius addition).
Behaviour weights, from the Stage-2 training interaction sequences only:
  count lag-1 pairs (i_t, i_{t+1}) with weight 1.0 and lag-2 pairs (i_t, i_{t+2}) with weight 0.5, over all training sequences truncated at the Stage-2 split boundary;
  p_ij = C_ij / sum_k C_ik ;  popularity p_j = (#occurrences of j)/(#training events);
  adjusted  w_ij = (p_ij / p_j^{1/2}) / sum_k (p_ik / p_k^{1/2}), over {j : C_ij > 0, j != i}.
Step: v_i = sum_j w_ij log_{z_i}(z_j) ;  eta_i = sum_j w_ij^2 ;  b_i = exp_{z_i}(eta_i v_i).
Quantize: feed b_i into the existing curved residual chain (3 levels x 256 codewords, CODEBOOK_DIM 32) and train the codebooks exactly as the baseline does for 3000 epochs.
Switches (all present in code, only both-on trained): BEHAV_SMOOTH in {False,True}; CURV_C in {1.0, 0.0}; both-on = (True, 1.0). BEHAV_SMOOTH=False sets eta_i = 0 for all i, hence b_i = z_i exactly. CURV_C = 0.0 replaces every exp/log by its flat limit, i.e. z_i = kappa t_i, log_z(w) = w - z, b_i = z_i + eta_i sum_j w_ij (z_j - z_i), and the residual chain becomes a flat RQ-VAE; that is the Euclidean counterfactual, with the same weights and the same eta.

ideas.title: Concentration-scaled geodesic step toward each item's behaviour-successor barycentre, taken before level-1 quantization (items move, codebooks do not).

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: C is replaced by the frozen Stage-1 text kNN graph and v_i by the PCA lift of the frozen text embedding, so the tree, the fanout and the anchors are text-derived; the geodesic hyperplanes, the Poincare distances and the fixed anchors are kept. The SID then has no interaction information at all.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Train-graph spectral ball, geodesic (Klein-affine) separators, gyro-barycentric anchors, Poincare-distance logits, hierarchical cross-entropy, straight-through text reconstruction, 3 SID levels of at most 32 prefix-local ids, 3000 Stage2 epochs on four cards, then the frozen Stage3 protocol. This is the only arm that is trained.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: The same behaviour graph, spectral embedding and ball coordinates are kept, but the separators are ordinary affine hyperplanes in the Poincare coordinates v (not the Klein chart) and the assignment logits are -||v - a_c|| with Euclidean centroid anchors; the split acceptance test is unchanged. Same code path, curved operator replaced by its Euclidean counterpart.
ideas.behavior_computation: For every session in the train split, count consecutive pairs (i_t, i_{t+1}) into C; row-normalise nothing (raw counts), build the symmetric normalised adjacency A = D_r^{-1/2} (C+C^T) D_c^{-1/2}, take the top m=32 eigenpairs (lambda_k, u_k) by magnitude with Lanczos, set g_i = (lambda_k u_k[i])_{k=1..32}, rho_i = ||g_i||, r_i = r_max * clip(rho_i / q90(rho), r_min/r_max, 1) with r_max = artanh(0.9) and r_min = artanh(0.2), and v_i = r_i g_i/||g_i||, v_i = 0 if rho_i = 0. All of this is computed from train interactions only, before Stage2 starts, and is frozen.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed consecutive-item transitions from the train split only, aggregated as C[i,j] and symmetrised into an undirected behaviour graph W = C + C^T.
ideas.cost_estimate: Stage2 per-step is not larger than baseline: level-1 distance is 4096x32 anchors, levels 2 and 3 gather only the parent's <=32 children, i.e. 4096*3*32*32 ~ 1.3e7 multiply-adds per step versus the baseline dense 4096x256 codebook matmuls, so expect 0.145 s/epoch to become about 0.14-0.16 s/epoch, i.e. 420-480 s for 3000 epochs at 24 steps/epoch on 4096-item batches. One-off preprocessing: sparse Lanczos top-32 on a ~24.5k x 24.5k transition matrix, ~20-40 s; recursive splits and Klein-bisector iterations over at most 32k nodes, ~2-6 min; ~20 Karcher iterations over 24.5k points in 32 dims, <10 s. Total wall clock +5 to +15 percent, all of it before the first Stage2 step; Stage3 decode cost is identical because the SID length and vocabulary width are unchanged.
ideas.coupling_equation: L_sid = -(1/3) sum_{l=1..3} log softmax_{c in Ch(p_{l-1}(i))} ( -d_P( exp_0(f_theta(x_i)), a_c ) ), with a_c = KarcherMean_{B^32}( { v_j : j in S_c } ) and the partition {S_c} defined by argmin over Klein-affine geodesic hyperplanes of cut_W(A,B) subject to cut <= E_null[cut] - 2 sigma_null.
ideas.coupling_path: train transitions -> symmetrised behaviour graph -> Fiedler coordinate inside each node -> geodesic hyperplane (Klein-affine bisector) -> node fanout and leaf membership -> gyro-barycentric anchor per child -> Poincare-distance logits over that parent's children -> hierarchical cross-entropy -> gradient into the encoder. Removing behaviour changes which hyperplanes exist and which children exist; removing the curved operator replaces sphere-arc separators and Poincare logits by planes and Euclidean norms, which changes both the leaves and the argmax; either removal changes the emitted SIDs.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: The claim is that behaviourally coherent prefixes plus capacity where behaviour is heterogeneous give the Stage3 beam more usable conditional structure than a text-reconstruction partition, and that the extra effective depth (leaves up to 32^3 instead of 2201 triples) is not paid for in prediction difficulty. It is worth keeping if, in the single run, leaves per item count drops well below the round-one 14 items per deepest prefix, the prefix-conditional concentration of the training successor distribution rises (recorded, not gated), Stage2 reconstruction stays finite with no prefix-count collapse (level-1 children used >= 75 percent of allocated children at every level over the last 200 epochs), and Stage3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: It acts in SID construction (the partition is made of geodesic hyperplanes and its nodes are gyro-barycentres) and in quantisation every training step (the assignment logits are exact Poincare distances, differentiated back into the encoder). It does not act in Stage3.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Constant negative curvature c = 1 (fixed, not tuned, because a tangent rescaling by 1/sqrt(c) reproduces c=1 exactly): the exact Poincare distance d_P(x,y) = arcosh(1 + 2||x-y||^2 / ((1-||x||^2)(1-||y||^2))), the exponential map at the origin exp_0(z) = tanh(||z||) z/||z||, its inverse log_0, the Karcher/gyro-barycentre in the ball, and the geodesic hyperplane represented as an affine hyperplane in the Klein chart k = 2p/(1+||p||^2).
ideas.key_change: The RQ-VAE assignment is replaced by a descent through a fixed behaviour-built hyperbolic tree: at each of three levels the encoder output competes only among its parent's children, scored by exact Poincare distance to the children's fixed gyrobarycentric anchors, and trained by hierarchical cross-entropy; the tree's fanout and leaves come from directed-train-transition cut tests on geodesic hyperplanes.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition counts C, the spectral embedding, the ball coordinates, the tree, the fanout, the leaf membership and the anchors are computed in a single pass over the train split interactions, written to a frozen artefact, and never recomputed or updated during Stage2 or Stage3. No validation or test interaction enters C, the SVD, the split criterion, the anchor, or any statistic that affects the SID; validation and test interactions are read only by the frozen Stage3 evaluation after the SIDs are frozen, and the behavioural diagnostics are computed from train-fold transitions only so that they cannot even indirectly select anything.
ideas.motivation: Round one produced 2201 distinct 3-token triples for 24556 items, so ~11 behaviourally different items share one SID and the generative model cannot separate them; the curvature and the prefix structure were also decoupled, and the curved reconstruction objective killed the encoder. The problem addressed is that prefix capacity and prefix membership are allocated by text-reconstruction geometry, not by what users actually do next.
ideas.novelty: Earlier rounds changed codebook positions (successor-weighted Frechet), per-level curvature, radial rank from entropy/context entropy, cones, per-level boosts and residuals, all on a shared RQ codebook with 256 codes per level. Here the SID is a *tree path in a behaviour-cut geodesic partition*, the token alphabet is prefix-local (the same id at level 2 means different items under different parents), and the fanout of every node is decided by a degree-preserving-null significance test on directed train transitions. So the mechanism changes *which items may share a token and how many distinct triples exist*, i.e. the prefix structure and the SID capacity allocation, not the positions inside a fixed triplet of codebooks. Geometry is not a curvature value (curvature is fixed at c=1 because it is a gauge) but the shape of the separator: geodesic hyperplanes, affine in the Klein chart, sphere arcs in the Poincare model, which cut the item set differently from any Euclidean plane in the Poincare coordinates.
ideas.observables: SID assignment: number of leaves, per-level fanout histogram, items per leaf, number of distinct used triples, and the fraction of items whose triple is unique; gradient/parameter update: mean ||z|| over training (must not drift toward 0), gradient norm reaching the encoder through d_P, and per-level child-usage entropy over the last 200 epochs; prefix behaviour predictability: the train-split conditional entropy of the successor's level-1 code given the source item's prefix, and the held-out-train-transition prefix hit rate; Stage3: test_recall@10, recall@5, ndcg@10 over 57439 queries.
risks: Prefix-local ids force one shared token embedding to serve several parent contexts, which can make Stage3 harder to learn and could lose more than the capacity gain; near-unique leaves can destroy the prefix sharing that lets TIGER generalise and may lower recall@10; the 2-sigma null test may accept too few splits on a sparse transition graph, degenerating to a shallow tree and re-creating collisions; tail items with no transitions get degenerate ball coordinates; the hierarchical CE and the text reconstruction can fight, and the straight-through path may let the encoder satisfy CE while the decoder loses text fidelity.
ideas.safeguards: clamp ||x||, ||a|| <= 1-1e-5 and denominators 1-||x||^2 >= 1e-6; clamp the arcosh argument to >= 1+1e-7; if ||z|| < 1e-8 set v = 0 and let the logits be -d_P(0, a_c) = -2 artanh(||a_c||), which is finite because anchors are clamped; log mean ||z|| and the per-level child-usage entropy every 50 epochs and treat a monotone decay of ||z|| toward 0 together with a usage entropy toward 0 as the round-one collapse signature (the loss is maximal at the origin, so this should not trigger, but it is the check); nodes with no significant split become leaves and their members share the prefix, which is intended and is not repaired by forcing splits; items with rho_i = 0 get v_i = 0 and are placed by the hyperplane sign with the deterministic tie-break "first child"; empty child sets are pruned before anchor computation; all tree and anchor quantities are recomputed once from the frozen artefact hash so that Stage2 and Stage3 read bit-identical SIDs; no weight, temperature, clip bound or curvature is swept: the only scalar constants are lambda = 1 for the two summed losses (equal-scale documented default), tau = 1 in curvature-normalised units, c = 1 by gauge, r_min/r_max = artanh(0.2)/artanh(0.9), the 2-sigma one-sided test, depth 5 and b = 32, all derived from N, the SID length and the vocabulary width.
ideas.spec_equations: 1) A = D_r^{-1/2}(C+C^T)D_c^{-1/2}; top-32 eigenpairs; g_i; r_i; v_i = r_i g_i/||g_i||. 2) For a node S: W_S = W[S,S], L_sym = I - D_S^{-1/2} W_S D_S^{-1/2}, f = eigenvector of the second smallest eigenvalue; A = {f<0}, B = S\A. 3) Klein k_x = 2x/(1+||x||^2); kbar_A = mean(k_x, x in A), kbar_B likewise; w = kbar_A - kbar_B, t = 0.5(||kbar_A||^2 - ||kbar_B||^2); repeat assignment x -> A if <k_x,w> > t, B otherwise, with centroid recomputation, at most 5 times, break on a stable sign pattern. 4) Null test: V = sum_{i in S} d_i, m = vol(A)vol(B)/(V-1), s2A = sum_{i in A} d_i^2, s2B likewise, Var = m - s2A s2B/V^2, accept iff cut_W(A,B) <= m - 2 sqrt(max(Var,0)) and cut_W(A,B) >= 1 and |A|,|B| >= 1. 5) Recurse while depth < 5 and |S| >= 2 and the test passes; n_min = max(2, ceil(N/b^3)) = 2 with b = 2^ceil(log2(N^{1/3})) = 32; node children are numbered 0..k-1 and that number is the token id at that level. 6) Anchor: a <- exp_{a}( (1/n) sum_i log_{a}(v_i) ) for 20 iterations from a = mean(v_i), then clamp ||a|| <= 1-1e-5. 7) v = exp_0(f_theta(x)); logits = -d_P(v, a_c); L = L_text(z + sg(sum_l log_0(a_{p_l(i)}) - z)) + L_sid. 8) Forward pass pseudocode: for l in 1..3: Cands = children(parent_{l-1}); s = -d_P(v, a[Cands]); p_l = argmax s; loss += -log softmax(s)[p_l]; token_l = index of p_l among Cands.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: the train-split session list, the item index (24556 training items), the frozen Stage-1 text features x_i, the codebook dimension 32, the SID length 3, and the vocabulary width 256. The tree builder consumes (C, v, W) and returns the node table (parent, child index, member set, anchor a_c, depth), which is frozen. The encoder consumes x_i and returns z_i in R^32; the quantiser consumes (z_i, node table) and returns the triple of prefix-local token ids and the softmax probabilities used by the loss; the decoder consumes the straight-through quantised tangent vector and returns the reconstructed text features.

specification.text: Build once from train transitions C: symmetric normalised adjacency, top-32 spectral embedding, lift to the ball as v_i = r_i * g_i/||g_i||. Recursively split each node S by (i) the Fiedler vector of the normalised behaviour Laplacian on S, (ii) the affine (Klein) bisector of the two sides' Klein centroids, (iii) re-assignment by the sign of that affine form until stable, and accept the split only if cut <= E_null[cut] - 2*sigma_null. Recurse to depth 5 per SID level (fanout <= 32) and 3 SID levels. Anchors a_c = Karcher barycentre of {v_i : i in child c}, then frozen. Encoder z = f(x), v = tanh(||z||) z/||z||; logits at level l are -d_P(v, a_c) over the children of the parent chosen at level l-1; loss = text reconstruction (straight-through) + sum_l -log softmax(-d_P). Stage3 unchanged: three tokens per item from a <=32-id-per-level alphabet inside the existing 256-token vocabulary.

ideas.title: Behaviour-cut geodesic prefix tree with prefix-local SID ids and hyperbolic soft-assignment (fixed gyrobarycentric anchors)

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: use_behaviour_anchor = False: set v_p(b) uniform over S_p (equivalently b_p := a_p), so Delta_p = 0, theta_p = 0, all R_p = I and the assignment is exactly the baseline; wired in code, never trained.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the full run above, the only arm actually trained: 3000 Stage-2 epochs on four GPUs at global batch 4096, then the frozen 150-epoch Stage 3.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: use_hyperbolic = False: set theta_p := 0 and use the Euclidean distance and Euclidean exp/log, so the holonomy channel is provably zero and the quantizer reduces to the Euclidean RQ-VAE; wired in code, never trained.
ideas.behavior_computation: Directed consecutive-pair counts T[a,b] from Stage-2 training user histories only, row-normalised to P(b|a); prefix successor weight v_p(b) = mean over i in S_p of P(b|i); b_p = psi(sum_b v_p(b) z_b). Nothing else is read, and T is built once before training starts.
ideas.behavior_signal: Prefix-conditioned successor displacement - the training-only distribution over next items given each item, aggregated over the items of a prefix, compared with the prefix's own text position.
ideas.cost_estimate: Static pass at epoch 0 plus refresh every 100 epochs: 256 active prefixes x 3 levels, each O(32-d log/exp + a 32x32 rotation), so about 1e6 flops per pass, i.e. milliseconds. Per step the extra work is rotating the codebooks of the prefixes present in a 4096-item batch (at most ~32 prefixes x 256 codes x 32 dims = 2.6e5 flops) plus one Poincare distance matrix instead of a Euclidean one (4096 x 256 x 32 = 3.4e7 flops): expected +5 to +10% on the 0.145 s/epoch baseline, so ~0.152-0.160 s/epoch and 585-605 s for the 3000-epoch, 24-step, 4-GPU Stage 2. Stage 3 is untouched (frozen 150-epoch protocol).
ideas.coupling_equation: c'_{p,k} = exp^{c=1}_{a_p}( R_{e1,e2}(theta_p) log^{c=1}_{a_p}(c_k) ), with theta_p = -Area_c( o, a_p(w_behaviour), b_p(w_behaviour) ) and b_p = psi(sum_b v_p(b) z_b), v_p(b) proportional to sum_{i in S_p} P_train(b|i).
ideas.coupling_path: transition counts -> successor anchor b_p -> hyperbolic triangle (origin, a_p, b_p) -> area -> holonomy angle theta_p -> rotation R_p of the level-l codebook -> assignment k_i -> SID token -> Stage 3. Removing behaviour sets b_p := a_p, the triangle degenerates, Delta_p = 0, theta_p = 0 and every prefix keeps the baseline codes; removing geometry sets Delta_p := 0 (Euclidean holonomy is trivial) and the assignment becomes the Euclidean baseline. Neither term survives alone.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If deep-prefix aliasing is the binding capacity problem and behaviour adds directional information only where a prefix's successors drift, then rotating just the drifting prefixes' frames should raise the number of distinct L3 triples above 2,201 and thin the items-per-triple tail, and lift Stage 3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 by giving the generator finer distinctions among the frequently queried items. Observable in distinct L3 triples, the 95th percentile of items-per-triple, per-prefix conditional entropy of the L3 code, and finally test_recall@10 / recall@5 / ndcg@10 on the frozen 57,439-query protocol.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside quantization, at every RQ level, immediately before the nearest-codeword assignment and inside the decode of the assigned code: the shared codebook of a prefix is expressed in that prefix's own holonomy-rotated frame.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball with FIXED curvature c = 1 (gauge-fixed, no learned curvature), using the Poincare distance, the log/exp maps at a_p, and the geodesic-triangle area via Gauss-Bonnet, whose holonomy is -Area. The rotation R_p is itself a hyperbolic isometry about a_p.
ideas.key_change: For every prefix p we build a successor anchor b_p by propagating the frozen text embeddings through the row-normalised training transition matrix, and a text anchor a_p from the prefix's own items; the hyperbolic area of (origin, a_p, b_p) sets an angle theta_p, and the level's shared 256-codeword codebook is rotated by theta_p about a_p before nearest-neighbour assignment inside p. Prefixes whose items lead where they already are get theta_p = 0 and keep their baseline codes; prefixes whose successors drift away get a distinct, area-determined frame, which de-aliases the deep triples.
ideas.leakage_boundary: T, v_p, a_p and b_p use only Stage-2 training histories and the frozen Stage-1 text embeddings; the prefix sets S_p come from the model's own training-time assignment. Validation and test sequences are never touched: the frames are a deterministic function of (training transitions, frozen text vectors), so no item's SID can depend on a held-out interaction and no test query can alter theta_p or c'_{p,k}.
ideas.motivation: Round one showed where the problem is flat. Level 1 already uses essentially all 256 codewords, while levels 2 and 3 produce only 1,769 and 2,201 distinct prefixes over 24,556 items (about 11 items per deepest triple). The ranking cannot move unless the PREFIX STRUCTURE moves, i.e. unless items sharing an (L1,L2,L3) triple stop sharing it. At the same time issue 126 says the radial coordinate is only group compactness and that permuting radii destroys the correlation, while Gromov-delta and ancestor-depth weighting actively hurt. So the usable behaviour signal is a CONTRAST/direction signal, and the usable geometric object is not a radius but a frame. This idea takes the one curvature-specific quantity with no Euclidean analogue - the holonomy, the rotation a tangent vector picks up when parallel-transported around a closed geodesic loop - and uses it to orient the residual codebook of every prefix, driven by where that prefix's training-only successors actually go.
ideas.novelty: Not a weighted assignment, not a Frechet codebook update, not a per-level curvature, not an entropy-ranked radius, not Gromov-delta weighting. Curvature is FIXED at c = 1 (gauge-fixed, exactly as issue 126(b) requires) and nothing about curvature is learned; what is measured is the AREA of a geodesic triangle (origin, prefix text anchor, prefix successor anchor), and that area becomes a holonomy rotation of the code frame in the 2-plane spanned by the two anchors' disagreement. The mechanism is provably inert (identical to the baseline assignment) when behaviour adds no directional information, and it is also inert in the Euclidean limit, so it cannot be a behaviour suffix on an unchanged quantizer. No earlier round used holonomy or a frame rotation.
ideas.observables: distinct L3 prefixes (baseline 2,201), distinct L2 prefixes (baseline 1,769), the items-per-triple distribution and its 95th percentile, per-prefix conditional entropy of the L3 code, the fraction of prefixes with |theta_p| > 1e-3, per-epoch reconstruction loss, SID coverage (all 24,556 items, 251 L1 codewords), and Stage 3 test_recall@10 (target > 0.065; baseline 0.0679; round-one 0.05439), recall@5 and ndcg@10.
risks: (a) A rigid per-prefix rotation can act like a relabelling: if the level-3 codebook is near rotationally symmetric the partition barely changes and triples shift without gaining information. (b) If successor drift is dominated by global popularity, v_p is nearly identical for every prefix, all theta_p cluster near one value, and the mechanism degenerates to a single global relabelling. (c) Large areas give large rotations that scatter codes arbitrarily and can hurt. (d) The 100-epoch refresh makes frames piecewise constant, so late prefix drift is only partly tracked. (e) Single run: the +/-0.003 seed noise on recall cannot be separated from a real gain.
ideas.safeguards: map every vector with psi and clip ball norms to 1 - 1e-3; clamp every cosh argument to [0, 30] and every cos(alpha) to [-1 + 1e-7, 1 - 1e-7] before arccos; clip Delta_p to [0, pi] and set theta_p := 0 whenever any side is below 1e-8, any value is non-finite, or |theta_p| < 1e-6; wrap theta to (-pi, pi]; orthonormalise (e1,e2) by Gram-Schmidt and fall back to theta_p = 0 if ||e2|| < 1e-6; verify R_p orthogonality to 1e-5; assert the angle table is finite and log the fraction of prefixes with nonzero theta; break assignment ties on the smallest code index. Because the rotation is an isometry about a_p it cannot shrink the codebook toward the origin and cannot reproduce the round-one zero-residual collapse, and because the text geometry is frozen the trainable-encoder collapse path is unreachable.
ideas.spec_equations: see steps (1)-(7); d(u,v) = arcosh(1 + 2||u-v||^2/((1-||u||^2)(1-||v||^2))); exp_a(v) = tanh(||v||)(v/||v||), log_a its inverse, both in the c = 1 ball; cos(alpha) = (cosh B cosh C - cosh A)/(sinh B sinh C); Delta = pi - (alpha+beta+gamma); theta = -Delta; c'_{p,k} = exp_{a_p}(R_p log_{a_p}(c_k)); k_i = argmin_k d(z_i^l, c'_{p(i),k})^2.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: frozen text embeddings z_i in R^32 for 24,556 items, training transition counts T, the baseline 3 x 256 codebook, and the current prefix assignment. Outputs: for each active prefix and level a 256 x 32 rotated codebook c'_{p,.}, a per-prefix angle table theta (256 x 3), the SID matrix (24,556 x 3), and the prefix sets consumed by the next level.

specification.text:
Notation: z_i in R^32 is the frozen Stage-1 text embedding (identical to the baseline, no trainable encoder - the variant of round one that did not collapse). Ball map psi(z) = tanh(||z||/s) * z/||z|| with s = mean_i ||z_i|| over the 24,556 items (a derived, scale-relative constant), c = 1, ball radius 1.
(1) Behaviour matrix from the Stage-2 training split only: T[a,b] = number of consecutive pairs a->b in training histories. P(b|a) = T[a,b] / sum_b T[a,b] (zero-mass rows dropped).
(2) For prefix p with item set S_p: a_p = psi(mean_{i in S_p} z_i); v_p(b) = (1/|S_p|) sum_{i in S_p} P(b|i); b_p = psi(sum_b v_p(b) z_b). b_p lives in the SAME frozen text ball, so no cross-space projection is needed; behaviour enters only through v_p.
(3) Poincare distance d(u,v) = arcosh(1 + 2||u-v||^2 / ((1-||u||^2)(1-||v||^2))). Sides: A = d(o,b_p) (opposite the angle at a_p), B = d(o,a_p), C = d(a_p,b_p).
(4) Angles by the hyperbolic law of cosines: cos(alpha) = (cosh B cosh C - cosh A)/(sinh B sinh C), cyclically. Area Delta_p = max(0, pi - (alpha+beta+gamma)). Holonomy theta_p = wrap_to_(-pi,pi](-Delta_p) (Gauss-Bonnet, K = -1).
(5) Frame at a_p: e1 = log_{a_p}(b_p)/||log_{a_p}(b_p)|| (if ||log|| < 1e-8 then theta_p := 0); u_text = top principal direction of {log_{a_p}(z_i) : i in S_p}; e2 = orthonormalise(u_text - <u_text,e1> e1). R_p is the identity except on span(e1,e2), where it is the 2x2 rotation by theta_p.
(6) Rotated codebook for prefix p at level l: c'_{p,k} = exp_{a_p}( R_p log_{a_p}(c^l_k) ), k = 1..256. Assignment k_i = argmin_k d(z_i^l, c'_{p(i),k})^2 (ties to smallest k); residual z_i^{l+1} = log_{c'_{p,k_i}}(z_i^l) as in the baseline RQ. Level 1 uses p = root (a_p = origin), so its frame is untouched and all 256 codewords stay in play.
(7) Stage 2 then trains the frozen recipe on reconstruction of the frozen text geometry; only decoder/residual parameters move. Frames are computed once at epoch 0 and re-checked every 100 epochs for prefix-set drift.
Pseudocode: build T; psi all z; for l in 1..3: for each active prefix p: compute a_p, v_p, b_p, Delta_p, theta_p, R_p; build c'_{p,.}; assign all items in p; update prefix sets. Then run RQ-VAE training with these fixed per-prefix codebooks.

ideas.title: Behavioural-drift holonomy rotates the per-prefix code frame of the hyperbolic RQ-VAE, so where a prefix's successors drift decides which codewords its items receive.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: b_i := 0 for all items, so PT(w; rho, 0) = (0, w) = identity transport; the quantizer keeps the Lorentz distance but the child codebook no longer depends on where the parent sits or where behaviour points.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the full coupled run, one training run, 3000 epochs, four cards, frozen recipe, no arm trained with the switches off.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: replace exp, log, arccosh and the connection by their flat counterparts, i.e. PT = identity for every rho and b; the mechanism reduces exactly to the baseline RQ-VAE in R^32 with behaviour reading out to nothing.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the Stage-2 TRAINING split only: build the directed count matrix T_ij from consecutive (item, next item) pairs in every training sequence with a repeat-suppression window of 3; row-normalise, keep the top 20 successors by count per item, and drop any successor with mass below 1/20 of the row mass (2 fixed, derived defaults: the pruning threshold is the reciprocal of the retained support size, no sweep). With the frozen Stage-1 text embedding z^text of the baseline, define d_i = sum_j P_ij (z^text_j - z^text_i) and b_i = d_i / ||d_i||, with b_i = 0 when ||d_i|| < 1e-8.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-item transitions of the training sequences, converted into a per-item successor direction in the tangent space at the origin, used as the parallel-transport direction.
ideas.cost_estimate: Behaviour directions are precomputed once from the training split (sparse top-20 rows), so they add zero per-step cost. The extra per step is, per level, a 4096 x 256 x 33 transport plus a 4096 x 256 Lorentz distance, chunked at 512 items: about 1.0e8 elementwise ops and about 70 MB of transient memory per step at the frozen scale. Estimated 0.145 s/epoch -> 0.20-0.25 s/epoch, i.e. the 571 s Stage2 run becomes roughly 780-1050 s on the same four cards; Stage3 is untouched.
ideas.coupling_equation: k*_l(i) = argmin_k arccosh( max(1, <L(z), exp_{L(u)}( PT(C_{l,k}; ||u||, b_i) )>_L ) ), with b_i = normalise( sum_j P_ij (z^text_j - z^text_i) ) the behaviour term and PT / arccosh / exp the curved terms.
ideas.coupling_path: encoder output -> accumulated tangent u -> parent point P = exp_o(u) with distance rho -> behaviour direction b_i selects the geodesic -> PT moves every child codebook along that geodesic by rho -> Lorentz distance picks the child code -> straight-through gradient updates the encoder and codebooks -> the emitted L2/L3 token is the transported choice. Setting b_i = 0 makes the transport exactly the identity and the L2/L3 assignment Euclidean-in-tangent regardless of rho; replacing the connection with the trivial one makes transport the identity regardless of b_i, so each switch alone destroys the pathway.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If parent distance and behaviour direction genuinely shape the child partition, then the number of distinct L2 and L3 prefixes must rise materially above 1769 and 2201 while level-1 usage stays broad, the measured mean transport magnitude cosh(rho) must be clearly above 1 at L3, and Stage3 test_recall@10 must exceed the frozen 0.0679 baseline and the 0.065 gate from the single frozen run. If recall stays at 0.054 while the prefix counts rise, the mechanism is producing a finer but meaningless partition and is not worth keeping.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the residual quantizer's per-level assignment and straight-through residual, at levels 2 and 3 where the parent prefix has rho > 0; it shapes which child codeword an item receives and therefore the L2/L3 prefix structure itself.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: The Levi-Civita parallel transport of the Lorentz hyperboloid of constant curvature K = -1 (fixed, not trainable), with closed form PT(w; rho, b) = (w_par sinh rho, w_par cosh rho b + w_perp), plus the Lorentz geodesic distance used for the assignment.
ideas.key_change: Replace the level-l Euclidean nearest-codebook lookup by a lookup against a codebook that has been parallel-transported from the origin to the item's current parent prefix point, along the geodesic whose direction is the item's behaviour successor direction; the same transported vector is used for the straight-through residual, so the behaviour-and-curvature shaped partition is exactly the one the tokens encode.
ideas.leakage_boundary: T and b are computed only from the Stage-2 training sequences and the frozen Stage-1 text embedding, which itself never saw validation or test interactions; validation is used only for logging and Stage3 test queries are never read during Stage2, so no validation or test interaction can reach the transport directions, the codebooks or the encoder.
ideas.motivation: In a generative recommender the SID is consumed as a token sequence, so what matters is whether a parent prefix (L1, L2) leaves the true next item's child prefix predictable. Round one's SID was healthy but ranking-useless: level 1 saturated 251 of 256 codewords while levels 2 and 3 collapsed to 1769 and 2201 distinct prefixes, i.e. about fourteen items share every deepest prefix and the children carry almost no discriminative information about what a user actually does next. A Euclidean RQ assigns a child codeword as if every parent prefix lived at the same place, so the child partition is blind to how far out in the hierarchy the parent already sits and to where the user's behaviour is heading from that item.
ideas.novelty: The codebook is made parent-dependent by GEODESIC PARALLEL TRANSPORT, not by radial reweighting, not by Fréchet centroid updates, not by per-level curvature control, not by Gromov-delta or ancestor-depth weights, and not by cone constraints. Curvature enters as the Levi-Civita connection of the Lorentz model (transport is the identity in the flat limit), behaviour enters only as the transport DIRECTION, and they meet in a single line: the level-l codebook seen by item i is PT over the geodesic o -> P_{l-1} of C_l with direction b_i. Because transport is an isometry it cannot shrink codes toward the origin, which is the exact collapse mode that killed round one's curved residual objective.
ideas.observables: distinct L2 prefix count (baseline 1769), distinct L3 prefix count (baseline 2201), L1 codeword usage (baseline 251/256), the per-level mean and 95th percentile of cosh(rho) and of the transport's along-behaviour fraction |w_par|/||w||, the frozen prefix-transition probe's accuracy at predicting the empirical next-item prefix from the parent prefix, the train reconstruction loss trajectory, and Stage3 test_recall@10 / @5 / ndcg@10.
risks: The per-item effective codebook may become so item-specific that assignment turns arbitrary, which would raise prefix counts but destroy prefix semantics and drop recall below 0.054; deep prefixes (rho up to 5) give cosh(rho) up to 74 and can amplify the along-behaviour component until the transported codebook is dominated by b_i, so rho must be clamped and monitored; the behaviour direction derived from frozen text geometry may be too noisy for rare items (row mass below the pruning threshold), where the mechanism degenerates to identity transport.
ideas.safeguards: fixed curvature K = -1 (gauge, never trained); ||z|| clipped to 5 and rho clipped to [0, 5] so cosh(rho) <= 74; Lorentz arccosh argument clamped to >= 1 with an epsilon inside the sqrt; codebook rows re-normalised to unit Euclidean norm after every optimiser step so their scale cannot drift; b_i zeroed when ||d_i|| < 1e-8 and for items with an empty successor row; assignment chunked at 512 items to bound transient memory; a NaN/Inf guard that falls back to identity transport for the affected step; the along-behaviour fraction is logged every epoch so a transport that has been swamped by b_i is visible rather than silent.

specification.text:
Curvature fixed at K = -1 (the gauge result of issue 126 says |K| is not identifiable, so it is fixed, never tuned).
Lorentz point of tangent u in R^32: L(u) = (sqrt(1+||u||^2), u).
exp_o(u) = L(u); log_o((x0,x)) = x.
Transport of a spatial code vector w along the geodesic o -> P with unit spatial direction b and length rho:
  w_par = <w,b>_E ; w_perp = w - w_par*b
  PT(w; rho, b) = (w_par*sinh(rho), w_par*cosh(rho)*b + w_perp) in (time, space) tangent coordinates at P.
This is an isometry: <PT(w),PT(w)>_L = ||w||^2.
Per item i with encoder output z (clipped, ||z||<=5) and precomputed behaviour direction b_i:
  u <- 0 ; codes <- []
  for l = 1..3:
      rho <- ||u|| ; P <- L(u)
      for k in 1..256: Q_k <- exp_{P}( PT(C_l[k]; rho, b_i) )

      codes.append(k*) ; u <- u + C_l[k*]                       (straight-through: gradient copies dB/dz)
  reconstruction loss on z_hat from the sum of C_l[k*]; commitment loss unchanged from the frozen baseline.

objective:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.

Round two. One mechanism along the chain: user behaviour data -> behaviour graph -> tree-structure check -> behaviour item embedding -> Gromov delta -> hyperbolic curvature -> text embedding into a hyperbolic RQ-VAE -> behaviour supervision -> SID -> Stage3 -> test_recall@10. The target is a real test_recall@10 above 0.065 from one frozen four-GPU Stage2 run and one frozen Stage3 run. The baseline for this round is the previous complete mechanism, the tree TIGER_CURV-RESID-CONTRAST (a copy of it is the starting point; the framework resolves it).

WHAT ROUND ONE MEASURED, and what the new proposals must take as given:
1. The mechanism in the baseline ran the whole loop: Stage2 3000 epochs in 571 s at 0.145 s/epoch, a HEALTHY SID (251 L1 prefixes out of 256 codewords, 1769 L2, 2201 L3, every item covered), Stage3 150 epochs under the frozen protocol. Its result was test_recall@10 = 0.05439, test_recall@5 = 0.0360, test_ndcg@10 = 0.0296 over 57,439 queries. That is BELOW the 0.065 gate and below the frozen baseline's own 0.0679. So the round-one mechanism is a NEGATIVE result on the recommendation metric and must not be simply reused or re-tuned.
2. The collapse lesson: in round one a trainable encoder feeding the curved chain collapsed twice (two prefixes per level, then one), because the curved assignment objective has its minimum at the origin (a zero residual). The only variant that trained was one that quantized the FROZEN Stage-1 text geometry, where the ball configuration cannot collapse but the mechanism then has no influence on the encoder at all. Any new mechanism must be checked against this failure mode and must keep its signal reaching the tokens.
3. The offline diagnostics of issue 126, which the proposals must respect: (a) the interaction graph is tree-like and a degree-preserving rewiring of it is EXACTLY as tree-like, so 'the data is a tree' is not available as a premise; (b) curvature is a gauge, scaling the tangent by 1/sqrt(c) reproduces curvature 1 exactly; (c) on the 107 confirmed SID/recall pairs the metrics that predict Recall are behaviour-CONTRAST metrics and their Euclidean controls match or beat the hyperbolic forms (HBAA plain +0.7104, Euclidean +0.7170, unweighted four-point agreement +0.6593), while Gromov-delta weighting and ancestor-depth weighting hurt by 0.12 and 0.075; the radial term is group compactness (91% with the dispersion, 0.98 with the distance to a random point), and a full permutation of the radius values collapses the correlation to the baseline.
4. Capacity observation from round one: the quantizer is 3 levels of 256 codewords and CODEBOOK_DIM is 32, against 24,587 items; level one uses essentially every codeword and levels two and three produce only 1,769 and 2,201 distinct prefixes, i.e. roughly fourteen items per prefix at the deepest level. A mechanism that wants to change the ranking has to change the PREFIX STRUCTURE, not only the codebook positions.

HARD CONSTRAINTS: a single formal training run per candidate (3000 epochs, four-GPU DDP, global batch 4096, frozen recipe), no ablation arms, no hyperparameter tuning, no seed sweeps; every constant derivable a priori. The behaviour-off / geometry-off / both-on switches must exist in the code and be wired correctly, but only the both-on arm is trained. Stage3 keeps its frozen protocol. Stage2->Stage3 admission is technical validity only; test_recall@10 > 0.065 is the final judgement. A negative result is a legitimate outcome and must be recorded with its numbers.

papers.abstract: The success of models operating on tokenized data has heightened the need for effective tokenization methods, particularly in vision and auditory tasks where inputs are naturally continuous. A common solution is to employ Vector Quantization (VQ) within VQ Variational Autoencoders (VQVAEs), transforming inputs into discrete tokens by clustering embeddings in Euclidean space. However, Euclidean embeddings not only suffer from inefficient packing and limited separation - due to their polynomial volume growth - but are also prone to codebook collapse, where only a small subset of codebook vectors are effectively utilized. papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.

papers.abstract: Machine learning algorithms have been shown to be highly effective in solving optimization problems in a wide range of applications.
